overview: This three-page file documents a June 1937 exchange between the U.S. Department of State, the Embassy in Tokyo, and the Consulate at Kobe concerning Japanese subsidies for ship construction and mail service. Two cross-reference sheets summarize the Department’s questions and Ambassador Joseph C. Grew’s response, while the complete telegram reports that the price and specification figures in Vice Consul Schuler’s April 22 shipping report came from the Japan Shipping Exchange rather than official sources. It also explains eligibility and allocations under Japan’s new ship-construction subsidy law, gives 1938 mail-subsidy appropriations, and promises that the law and detailed budget provisions will be forwarded by mail.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Japan and sender of the June 12 telegram from Tokyo

people.name: Schuler
people.role: U.S. Vice Consul; author of the shipping report dated April 22, 1937

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Department telegram No. 76 on Japanese shipping subsidies
subfiles.about: The sheet points to the Department’s inquiry about the calculations and legal basis for Japanese ship-construction and mail subsidies.
subfiles.summary: This filing note cross-references telegram No. 76 of June 7, 1937, in file 894.802/26a. The Department asked whether the ship prices and specifications in Vice Consul Schuler’s report were official, whether construction subsidies were generally or uniformly available to different types of vessels, and whether the calculations included all mail subsidies. It also requested budget figures and a translation of the new subsidy law.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet summarizing Grew’s telegram No. 156
subfiles.about: The sheet summarizes the reply concerning the sources, availability, and appropriations for Japanese shipping subsidies.
subfiles.summary: This filing note directs the reader to telegram No. 156 in file 894.802/27. It records that the ship prices and specifications were unofficial but came from the most reliable available source, and that the response discussed construction-subsidy eligibility and mail-subsidy appropriations. It notes that the text of the new law and the detailed budget provisions would follow by mail and identifies the information as originating with the Consulate at Kobe.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Grew transmitting Kobe’s answers on Japanese shipping subsidies
subfiles.about: Grew transmits the Kobe Consulate’s detailed answers to the Department’s questions about Japanese ship-construction and mail subsidies.
subfiles.summary: The Kobe Consulate reported that the prices and specifications in the April 22 shipping report were not official, but were drawn from the Japan Shipping Exchange’s monthly publication. Construction subsidies were available only for cargo and combination vessels, with combination vessels receiving ¥44,693,567 of the total ¥50,693,567 allocation. Mail subsidies appropriated for 1938 totaled ¥9,550,736, of which ¥5,135,736 had been allotted by the date of the April 22 report. The text of the new law and its budgetary provisions was to be sent separately by mail.

interest: The file is useful because it preserves both the bureaucratic cross-reference trail and the substantive diplomatic telegram, showing how the State Department checked the reliability and comparability of economic intelligence received from its consular officers. The telegram provides unusually precise figures for Japan’s allocation of construction and mail subsidies and clarifies the distinction between cargo ships and the favored combination vessels. It also identifies the Japan Shipping Exchange’s monthly publication as the best available source when official ship-price and specification data could not be obtained.
